title.value: Learning to Cut by Looking Ahead: Cutting Plane Selection via Imitation Learning
title.justification: The title is a direct reference to the core concept of the paper, which is the use of imitation learning to improve the selection of cutting planes in mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) problems.
title.quote: Learning to Cut by Looking Ahead: Cutting Plane Selection via Imitation Learning

extractions.description: This paper introduces a new neural architecture called NeuralCut, which utilizes imitation learning to optimize the selection of cutting planes in mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) problems. By approximating a greedy lookahead selection rule, the neural model aims to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of cut selection in MILP solvers. The approach shows potential application in various MILP contexts, including neural network verification.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on optimization techniques for solving mathematical programming problems, specifically MILPs. While it may have indirect applications that impact environmental problems, these are not the central focus of the study. Therefore, it does not directly fall under any specific eco-responsible category.

secondary_categories.quote: After having determined the effectiveness of NeuralCut policies in the controlled environment, we now wish to investigate the impact that selecting good (bound-improving) cuts can have on a more complex and realistic solver setting.
